businessModel: Search-engine partnerships (Qwant in 26 regions, DuckDuckGo elsewhere); no ads or tracking
updateCadence: Point releases every 1-2 weeks on an ESR base; new ESR rebase about yearly
summary: Independent Firefox ESR fork. Waterfox 6.7 (Aug 2026) moved to ESR 153 with native tree-style vertical tabs, a built-in ad blocker panel, 12 palettes, restored legacy add-ons, no telemetry and AI disabled.
bestFor: Firefox users who want fewer Mozilla extras
People who want vertical tree tabs without an extension
Users who want no AI and no telemetry
notFor: People who want Firefox-level resources behind security patching
Those who need a polished mobile app
Anyone wanting workspaces or split view

pros.title: No telemetry, no AI
pros.detail: Zero telemetry, Safe Browsing endpoints disabled, Firefox 153 AI features turned off by default.

pros.title: Native tree-style tabs
pros.detail: Vertical tab strip with built-in tree support in 6.7, replacing the bundled add-on.

pros.title: Legacy add-on support
pros.detail: Restores restartless, overlay and restart-required add-ons alongside WebExtensions.

pros.title: Built-in ad blocker
pros.detail: 6.7 adds a dedicated blocker settings panel.

pros.title: Android app
pros.detail: Waterfox for Android (1.2.10, Gecko 159) is on Google Play.

cons.title: Behind on new Firefox features
cons.detail: ESR base means feature updates arrive only with the yearly rebase.

cons.title: Small team
cons.detail: Security patching depends on a small company shipping on top of Mozilla.

cons.title: Fewer tab-management tools
cons.detail: No workspaces or split view like Zen or Vivaldi.

faq.a: The Firefox 153 AI features are disabled by default and 6.7.4 added a switch to disable AI in search results.
Yes, Waterfox for Android is on Google Play (1.2.10, Gecko 159 as of late October 2026).

faq.q: Which Firefox is it based on?
faq.a: Waterfox 6.7 is built on Firefox ESR 153, up from ESR 140.

blocking: Built-in ad blocker plus ETP and uBO support

telemetry: Zero telemetry, Sentry removed on Android
extensions: Firefox add-ons, legacy add-ons, full MV2

mobileApps: Android app on Gecko 159, none for iOS
